surface_mechanism_description: Surface mediated exchange reactions between gaseous molecules and surface functional groups. Atomic layers are formed by sequential pulsing of the reactants, interposed with a purge step of an inert gas, to prevent vapour phase reaction. Surface reactions are self-limiting, resulting in controlled film growth with excellent conformality.
evidence: The basis of this method, first described by Suntola and Anston, 1 relies on surface mediated exchange reactions between gaseous molecules and surface functional groups. Atomic layers are formed by sequential pulsing of the reactants, interposed with a purge step of an inert gas, to prevent vapour phase reaction. Surface reactions are self-limiting, resulting in controlled film growth with excellent conformality. Typical growth rates of ALD films are less than one monolayer per cycle although specific precursor chemistries have been reported that provide molecular layer growth per cycle.
